briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Israel-Lebanon border conflict significantly escalated over the past 24 hours, leading the IDF to expand operations in southern Lebanon and Israel's Home Front Command to implement stricter civilian guidelines in northern communities. Concurrently, US-Iran negotiations remain in a precarious state, with President Trump reportedly toughening deal terms while Iran asserts full control over the Strait of Hormuz, prompting an ongoing naval blockade enforced by the US.

IRAN
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy has asserted full authority over traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, demanding permits for all vessels and warning against military interference. They reportedly deployed a new "27-Rajab" attack speedboat capable of firing 700km cruise missiles in Tehran's Enghelab Square during public rallies. IRGC claims to have shot down a US MQ-1 drone over Iranian territorial waters in the Persian Gulf and an "Orbiter" drone over Qeshm Island. An alleged Iranian ballistic missile strike on Kuwait's Ali Al-Salem air base reportedly injured five US military personnel and contractors, and seriously damaged two MQ-9 Reaper drones, with a US Air Force KC-135 tanker also sustaining shrapnel damage. Two members of an anti-Iran terrorist group were killed in clashes with Iranian border guards in West Azarbaijan. Economically, Iran's stock market reportedly saw a surge following positive news of potential resumption or expansion of operations, though senior officials warned of a severe economic and budget crisis. Politically, hardline factions continue to pressure against a deal with the US, despite President Pezeshkian and Speaker Qalibaf reportedly conveying the dire economic situation to the Supreme Leader. Negotiations with the US are ongoing, with Trump reportedly toughening terms related to the nuclear program and Strait of Hormuz, while Iran signals it will stick to its original position without major concessions. The Iranian Parliament is expected to vote soon on legislation formalizing Iran's management and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

ISRAEL
Hezbollah launched numerous rocket and drone barrages against northern Israel, targeting areas including Kiryat Shmona, Karmiel, Western Galilee, Safed, Upper Galilee, Rosh HaNikra, and Shomera. The IDF intercepted multiple rockets and drones, but some fell in open areas or caused direct hits, including in Kiryat Shmona (without casualties) and rockets falling near bathers in Nahariya. A suspected hostile aircraft intrusion in Rosh HaNikra was identified crossing from Lebanon, and an apparent Hezbollah drone struck a military zone near Shomera while another was intercepted. Two Israeli officers were reportedly seriously injured in a Hezbollah attack on a house in southern Lebanon. In response to the intensified attacks, the IDF has expanded operations in southern Lebanon and is preparing for increased fire. The IDF struck and destroyed a manned Hezbollah artillery command center in Burj al-Shamali, identifying secondary explosions indicating weapons. Prime Minister Netanyahu convened a security assessment. The Home Front Command has tightened guidelines for northern communities, canceling educational activities in "Confrontation Line" areas and several specific towns until June 1, 2026, 20:00 UTC, and restricting gatherings and closing beaches. Calls from opposition figures like Naftali Bennett and Gadi Eisenkot urged stronger military action against Hezbollah.

GAZA & WEST BANK
An Israeli airstrike in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza, killed Dr. Jamal Abu Aoun, head of the anaesthesia department at a local hospital. Additional Israeli airstrikes targeted a children’s playground in Gaza, causing casualties. Hamas announced it was invited to Egypt to renew talks on the "second phase" of a ceasefire agreement. Tony Blair indicated that talks with Hamas regarding the transfer of Gaza administration are set to begin in the coming days as part of an October 2025 ceasefire agreement. In East Jerusalem, a 21-year-old hotel employee was accused of spying for Hamas, providing information on security forces and soldiers, and allegedly expressing readiness to carry out a suicide attack.

LEBANON
Hezbollah conducted extensive rocket and drone attacks across northern Israel, including barrages on Kiryat Shmona, Karmiel, Western Galilee, Safed, Upper Galilee, Shomera, Rosh HaNikra, Metulla, Kfar Giladi, and Misgav Am. Hezbollah claims included targeting an Israeli command room in Avivim barracks with an Ababil drone, attacking Israeli army vehicles and soldiers in Zoutar al-Sharqiya with rockets and artillery, and destroying an Israeli Merkava tank in Yahmar al-Shaqif and targeting two Merkava tanks and a military force in Zoutar al-Sharqiya with drones and guided missiles. The IDF responded with strikes, destroying a manned Hezbollah artillery command center in Burj al-Shamali and a launcher used to fire rockets at northern Israel. Israeli forces also carried out airstrikes on Kfar Roummane and allegedly used white phosphorus shells in attacks on Nabatieh, Kfar Tibnit, Ali El-Taher, and Arnoun in southern Lebanon. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam stated that Israel is pursuing a "complete destruction" policy in Lebanon, violating sovereignty and causing forced displacement, but maintained that the decision for war and peace is a national one and negotiations remain the most appropriate path.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Barzani Charity Foundation in Iraqi Kurdistan sent over 1000 trucks of humanitarian aid to Deir ez-Zor, Syria, following a rise in Euphrates River water levels. A bridge connecting المراشدة and الباغوز in eastern Deir ez-Zor, near the Iraqi border, collapsed due to the Euphrates flood. In Iraq, four members of the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) were injured in a vehicle rollover in Muthanna province. The Iraqi football federation accused its former head, Adnan Darjal, of embezzling $500,000 gifted by Parliament Speaker Al-Halbousi, while Darjal denied the accusation. Adnan Muhammad Hammoud al-Jumaili, Deputy Oil Minister and Director General of Baiji Refineries, was arrested on corruption charges. Kata'ib Hezbollah criticized the US and British ambassadors for allegedly interfering in Iraq's domestic affairs.

GULF STATES
The US Central Command (CENTCOM) reported disabling a Gambia-flagged commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman that was attempting to breach the naval blockade against Iran and sail to an Iranian port, using a missile to disable its engine after over 20 warning shots. CENTCOM stated that US forces have disrupted five commercial ships and rerouted 116 since the blockade began. Oman's Maritime Security Center urged vessels to exercise caution due to a "floating object suspected to be a naval mine" west of the Strait of Hormuz traffic zone within Omani territorial waters. Qatar expressed opposition to permanent transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz but indicated temporary fees are negotiable. Saudi Arabia reportedly complained to the US that UAE attacks on Iran were increasing the risk of Iranian retaliation against regional energy facilities. There are unverified reports of Israeli troops stationed at a military complex in the UAE to operate Iron Dome batteries. Pakistan's leadership was credited by US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth for assisting in negotiations with Iran.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  Hezbollah intensified rocket and drone barrages on northern Israel, prompting widespread alarms and a direct hit in Kiryat Shmona.
2.  The IDF expanded operations in southern Lebanon, striking a Hezbollah artillery command center and preparing for increased cross-border fire.
3.  Israel's Home Front Command tightened civilian guidelines for northern communities, mandating school closures, gathering restrictions, and closing beaches.
4.  US President Trump reportedly toughened the terms of a potential deal with Iran, focusing on nuclear program details and the Strait of Hormuz.
5.  The IRGC Navy asserted full control over the Strait of Hormuz, requiring permits for all transiting vessels and warning against interference, while CENTCOM enforced the naval blockade by disabling a Gambia-flagged ship. Oman reported a suspected naval mine in the Strait's vicinity.
6.  An alleged Iranian ballistic missile attack on Kuwait's Ali Al-Salem air base resulted in 5 injured US personnel and significant damage to two MQ-9 Reaper drones.
7.  An Israeli airstrike killed the head of anaesthesia at a Gaza hospital and targeted a children's playground, causing casualties.
8.  Reports indicate a US F-15E Strike Eagle shot down in southwestern Iran in April was likely hit by a Chinese-made shoulder-launched missile.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks on the Israel-Lebanon front are critically high due to intensified Hezbollah attacks and the IDF's expanded operations and preparations for deeper engagement in southern Lebanon. The Strait of Hormuz remains a significant flashpoint, with Iran's assertive control contrasting with the US naval blockade and Oman's report of a suspected naval mine, creating a high risk of miscalculation or direct confrontation. The ongoing US-Iran negotiations, complicated by President Trump's toughened demands and Iran's resistance to concessions, mean the possibility of renewed US attacks against Iran remains an active threat, as stated by the US Secretary of Defense.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is one of cautious negotiation with Iran, with President Trump seeking a "great deal" but also ready for renewed attacks if diplomacy fails, as stated by Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. CENTCOM continues to enforce the naval blockade on Iran. In the Gulf, Qatar signaled flexibility on temporary transit fees for Hormuz but not permanent ones, while Saudi Arabia expressed concern to the US about UAE attacks on Iran potentially escalating regional energy facility risks. EU members have sanctioned Hamas leaders, a move condemned by Hamas. The UK's Minister Cooper is scheduled to visit China and India. Russia accused Ukraine of a drone attack on the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, while Ukraine claimed destruction of Russian Tu-142 aircraft. Reports suggested China might have supplied a shoulder-launched missile to Iran, though China denied providing military equipment. Turkey's opposition leader held a large protest in Ankara. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) warned that attacking nuclear sites is "like playing with fire" following the Zaporizhzhia incident.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are contradictions regarding the US naval blockade on Iran: President Trump reportedly stated it would be lifted, yet CENTCOM and Iranian sources confirm its continued enforcement. Claims by Arab networks about the IDF capturing the Beaufort fortress are unverified by official Israeli sources. Similarly, the alleged celebrations in Tehran over the assassination of Supreme Leader Khamenei and associated videos about his house being hit, emerging after a purported internet return, remain unverified and are highly suspicious for propaganda. The report that a US F-15E was shot down in Iran in April by a Chinese-made shoulder-launched missile is attributed to NBC but remains under investigation by US officials. Oman's report of a suspected naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz is unverified. Claims of joint Israeli-UAE strikes on Iran's South Pars gas field are also unverified. Iranian state media, such as Press TV, exhibits clear propaganda by framing Iran's actions as "assertive diplomacy" and "robust military readiness" while portraying US and Israeli actions as "terror." Conversely, anti-regime sources like Omid Dana demonstrate their bias by celebrating any perceived weakness of the Iranian regime or advances by its adversaries. Specific details on the extent of infrastructure damage in Lebanon from Israeli strikes (beyond the artillery command center) and precise casualty figures from all rocket/drone attacks are lacking, with many incidents reported as impacting "open areas."
